title: Plan a BFCM Campaign that Runs Itself with Rollouts
summary: Make BFCM easy on yourself and your team by scheduling these simple campaigns ahead of time using Shopify Rollouts
body_markdown:
Black Friday Cyber Monday isn't just a weekend anymore. It's a whole season that opens with a members-only sale in mid-November, peaks during the BFCM weekend, and carries on through gift guides and shipping cutoffs deep into December.


****


While merchants spend months planning all of it, success hinges on the small moments where someone has to make it real. Publishing the theme at midnight, changing prices, switching on the discount and then taking it all down Monday night without breaking the store that was working fine before.


****


A single slip-up can derail the entire weekend when a sale banner gets published with no sale behind it or when a customer at checkout is unable to locate their discount. Ultimately, teams opt to scale back their strategy, turning daily flash sales into a single weekend offer and leaving holiday planning for post-BFCM.


****


[Rollouts](https://admin.shopify.com/rollouts) moves that work forward in time. It lets you build, schedule, and launch store changes together, with theme customizations, discounts, and catalogs, all in a single timed release.


****


Build the campaign ahead of time, preview it market by market, and lay out the schedule. Each change is published on time and when the promotion ends, everything goes back the way it was. The plan stops being a checklist somebody has to work through and starts being the thing that runs.


****


Here are seven campaigns to consider this year, and what it takes to build each one.


## 1. Members-only early access promotion


Open the sale to email subscribers or loyalty members a day or two early, with the same offer or a slightly better one. Early access lets you assess demand before the main event, while there's still time to move inventory or rewrite the headline in the sale banner.


**Build it in Rollouts:**


- Create a rollout for early access. Add a member discount and theme changes to announce it.


- You can also choose to put the announcement behind a login on the customer account home.


- Schedule a second rollout for the public phase and set it to start the minute early access ends.


Members get their exclusive access, the public sale replaces it on the minute, and nobody manually publishes anything at 6am.


## 2. Every market on its own clock


Give each market the campaign it deserves. Deeper discounts where competition is fiercest, free local shipping where that matters more than a discount, and a start time that lands at midnight for the buyers.


For example, a UK sale can begin earlier and close at 11pm local. An Australian sale can run in AUD with its own discounts.


**Build it in Rollouts:**


- Create a single rollout. Add theme, discount and catalog changes for each market.


- Set rollout start and end times to follow the market's own time zone, so midnight means midnight where the buyers are located.


## 3. A new flash sale every morning


Run a steady sitewide offer all weekend, then drop a new flash sale every morning at the same hour. Offer 50% off a different bestseller each day, announced in advance so shoppers know when to show up.


It gives people a reason to come back tomorrow, and spreads demand across the whole weekend instead of one Friday spike.


**Build it in Rollouts:**


- Build the sitewide sale as one Rollout including theme changes and discounts.


- Build each daily flash as its own Rollout. Add that day's products, discounts, start time, and end time.


- You can schedule or run up to five Rollouts at once, so queue several days ahead.


Each flash ends on its own and drops the store back to the sitewide offer underneath. Set up the week on a Tuesday and watch it happen.


## 4. A full-price drop inside the sale


****


Launching something new during BFCM? Think of a limited run or a collaboration that isn't discounted at all. A full-price drop inside a discount weekend gives regulars a reason to look past the markdowns, and it pulls attention back to the store on a day when every inbox looks the same.


**Build it in Rollouts:**


- Create a catalog with your special product and pricing.


- Build one Rollout with that catalog and the theme announcement.


- Set the drop time.


The hero and the product launch together, without disturbing the sale running around it.


## 5. The mid-weekend second act


Plan a second act. If the weekend is running hot there's room to push harder, and if it's flat, waiting until Monday to respond burns the highest-traffic days of the year.


It might be the same offer a tier deeper, or something different entirely: a new hero banner, free shipping instead of a bigger discount, or bestselling products pushed to the front.


**Build it in Rollouts:**


- Build the second act as its own rollout, or maybe two, before the weekend starts.


- Preview it while there's time to look properly. Leave it unscheduled and ready.


- Launch it in one action when you see the trend.


Saturday's decision takes a minute to launch, not an afternoon, and you're shipping changes you already confirmed.


## 6. Black Friday out, Cyber Monday in


************ Treat Cyber Monday as its own campaign rather than an extension of Black Friday's. A different offer, different creative, and different products in the limelight.


This gives shoppers who bought on Friday a reason to come back Monday, while shoppers who held out get something new instead of the same banner four days running.


Schedule both campaigns to run back to back, with the handoff landing at midnight on Sunday.


**Build it in Rollouts:**


- Build the Black Friday rollout with its theme, catalog, and discounts.


- Set it to end Sunday at midnight.


- Build the Cyber Monday rollout with its own theme, catalog, and discounts.


- Set it to start the moment the first one ends.


The transition runs seamlessly at midnight on Sunday and no one stays awake to publish changes.


## 7. The holiday handoff


Decide now what happens on Tuesday, whether it’s a gift guide that replaces the sale creative, new shipping cutoff banners that count down to the last order date, or a Boxing Day offer with its own window.


**Build it in Rollouts:**


- Build the gift guide rollout to start right after Cyber Monday.


- Build the shipping cutoff banner with its own dates.


- Queue the Boxing Day sale as the earlier ones close.


- Give every rollout an end date.


Each rollout reverts on its own, so the store stays clean between campaigns. Your holiday campaign runs itself while you are packing and shipping orders from the busy weekend.


## Test the offer before running it live


Treat every campaign as an experiment before it goes live for all shoppers during the BFCM weekend. Rather than guessing which offer will land, run your discount, theme or catalog as an experiment to measure real world impact on conversion.


Rollouts lets you compare different strategies against your store and see which one converts better. Whether it’s a percentage discount, a BOGO offer, or testing a fresh holiday theme against your current store, Rollouts gives you the control to define your audience split, set the test duration and track results in real time. When the experiment ends, the results page highlights the winning variation and breaks down essential metrics like add-to-cart, reached checkout, conversion rate and bounce rate with clear confidence intervals so you can pick the right strategy based on data, not intuition.


## Plan the season. Let Rollouts run it on schedule.


These campaigns were always possible, but they were never practical. With Rollouts, you can now build them in October and the store launches them at midnight before BFCM, in every market, with nobody awake to hit publish.


****


[Rollouts](https://admin.shopify.com/rollouts) is available in your Shopify admin under Markets -> Rollouts. Build your first campaign this week and schedule it for the BFCM weekend.
